title: Power(n, x)
problemStatement: Solve “Power(n, x)” as posed in the A2Z sheet (Advanced Maths).
intuition: "Power(n, x)" uses bits as flags or XOR cancellations. Know shifts, masks, and that Python ints are unbounded (still discuss fixed-width in interviews).

approaches.title: Bit trick / mask approach
approaches.code:
def solve(n: int) -> int:
    # Skeleton for: Power(n, x)
    # Example idioms:
    # n & 1        -> parity
    # n & (n - 1)  -> drop lowest set bit
    # n & -n       -> isolate lowest set bit
    cnt = 0
    while n:
        n &= n - 1
        cnt += 1
    return cnt
approaches.time: O(#bits) or O(1) with hw instructions

complexity.time: O(#bits) or O(1) with hw instructions

commonMistakes: Arithmetic vs logical shifts in signed languages
patternRecognition: Powers of two, subset masks, XOR pairing
interviewInsight: State the invariant (e.g. XOR of pairs cancels) before the code for "Power(n, x)".
